The test image shows a corn **stem/stalk** that is bent or broken at a node. The node area appears darkened, and the stalk is tan-brown. This narrows candidates to the 11 stem classes.

Key observations:
- Stalk broken/bent at a node
- Darkened node area
- Dried, tan-brown tissue
- No visible purple coloration, no obvious black sclerotia, no smut galls

Top candidates: Physoderma_Stalk_Rot (black nodes, snaps at node), Diplodia_Stalk_Rot, Charcoal_Stalk_Rot, Anthracnose. Let me check references one per class.
Physoderma_Stalk_Rot reference shows green stalk with dark purplish-black spots. Test image looks different (dried, tan, no dark spots pattern). Let me check Diplodia_Stalk_Rot.
Very strong visual match. Diplodia_Stalk_Rot reference shows the same dried tan-brown stalk broken at a node in a field setting. Let me check other candidates to be thorough.
Charcoal_Stalk_Rot shows split-open stalks with shredded pith and black sclerotia. Very different from test image. Let me check Anthracnose stem and Bacterial_Stalk_Rot.

Anthracnose stem shows dark black lesions and reddish/pink discoloration on the stalk, very different from the test image. Let me check Bacterial_Stalk_Rot, Purple_Leaf_Sheath, Common_Smut, and one more Diplodia reference.

Bacterial_Stalk_Rot shows green plant with brown lesions. Purple_Leaf_Sheath shows green stalk with dark bordered lesions. Neither matches. Let me check Common_Smut stem and a second Diplodia_Stalk_Rot reference.

Common_Smut shows large galls, completely different. The second Diplodia_Stalk_Rot reference shows a close-up of a stalk with tan discoloration and small dark spots (pycnidia) embedded in the rind, consistent with the KB description. 

The test image is a very strong match for Diplodia_Stalk_Rot:
- Dried, tan-brown stalk broken/bent at a lower node
- Field setting with dried corn debris
- The node area shows darkening
- Small dark structures visible on the rind surface
- No charred appearance (rules out Charcoal), no purple/black lesions (rules out Anthracnose, Purple_Leaf_Sheath), no galls (rules out Common_Smut), no green stalk with dark spots (rules out Physoderma_Stalk_Rot)

The first Diplodia_Stalk_Rot reference (Corn_Disease_14.jpg) was nearly identical in appearance to the test image.
